anchors.citation: Hulme, A. (1982) The wave forces acting on a floating hemisphere undergoing forced periodic oscillations. J. Fluid Mech. 121:443-463.

identifier.why: no DOI/ISBN was verified in this sandbox; only the bibliographic citation (journal, volume, pages) is claimed

anchors.locator: J. Fluid Mech. 121:443-463, wave-free multipole expansion (the semi-analytical radiation/diffraction solution)

self_convergence.rule: reference self-converged when the 96 -> 144 term drift is at least 20x below the 5 % gate

anchors.transcribed_digits_note: NOT AVAILABLE (publisher paywall, no copy in the sandbox): no digit of Hulme's printed table is transcribed or hand-copied anywhere in this repository. Every reference number in results.json is computed at run time by the wave-free multipole series (recomputed and cross-checked by evidence.py), so 'ref' here means 'Hulme's semi-analytical method, re-derived and self-converged', not 'Hulme's printed digits' -- see docs/bem_hulme_hemisphere_case.md sections 1 and 6.

external_ledger_verdict.rule: reference_method.independent_of_repo_package must be true: a reference computed from this package's own solver shares the discretisation it is meant to judge
external_ledger_verdict.why: the reference lives in tensorbem.analytic.hulme_hemisphere_radiation (inside src/) and shares tensorbem.free_surface3d.wave_function_3d with the solver, so it cannot be registered as an external anchor; it is a LITERATURE_CLOSED_FORM re-derivation registered at case level

limits: NOT AVAILABLE (publisher paywall, no copy in the sandbox): no digit of Hulme's printed table is transcribed or hand-copied anywhere in this repository. Every reference number in results.json is computed at run time by the wave-free multipole series (recomputed and cross-checked by evidence.py), so 'ref' here means 'Hulme's semi-analytical method, re-derived and self-converged', not 'Hulme's printed digits' -- see docs/bem_hulme_hemisphere_case.md sections 1 and 6.

the reference series and the solver share tensorbem.free_surface3d.wave_function_3d, so agreement alone cannot catch a defect in that kernel; the independent axes are the third-party BEM crosscheck (capytaine, docs/capytaine_crosscheck.md) and the ka->0 rigid-lid even-mode series.
the third-party axis (evidence/independent.json) is what adjudicates a defect inside the shared wave-function kernel; it agrees with the reference to 3.36 % at worst over all six quantities
